results.title: AI Evaluation Metrics - Bias & Fairness — FRANKI T
results.content: # AI Evaluation Metrics - Bias & Fairness. Bias and fairness measure whether the AI model performs equitably across different demographic groups (e.g., age, gender, ethnicity) without systematically disadvantaging any group. This exploration of fairness and bias in AI systems forms the crux of this blog. Bias in artificial intelligence refers to the systemic errors in the outcomes produced by an AI system, which can be attributed to prejudiced assumptions made during the system's development stages, such as data collection, algorithm design, or model training. The AI model isn't inherently biased, but it reflects the biases in the data it was trained on. Fairness metrics are tools used to measure and mitigate bias in AI systems. They aim to quantify fairness, ensuring that AI models treat all individuals or groups equally, regardless of their underlying characteristics such as age, gender, race, or socioeconomic status. But understanding and implementing these metrics can be a nuanced and complex task, given the multifaceted nature of fairness and the inherent biases present in the data that train AI.

results.title: Fairness Measurement and Bias Mitigation in ML | Datatonic
results.content: In this blog post, we will explore the concept of fairness in Machine Learning, as well as the various methods used to measure, validate, and mitigate bias in ML models. #### How to Define Fairness in Machine Learning Models. Ideally, all ML models should perform fairly across all subgroups, but when there are so many definitions of “fairness”, how can we implement such standards in our Machine Learning models? * Demographic parity – the individuals across subgroups should have an equal proportion of positive outcomes (i.e. the sensitive feature is independent of the model’s prediction). To measure fairness in a Machine Learning model, we need to first identify any protected or sensitive attributes the data may contain that might cause bias in the model’s predictions. We can then compare and evaluate the performance metrics with the fairness metrics and set specific thresholds to identify if our model is biased towards any group in the sensitive attribute. Therefore it’s important to decide on an acceptable range of difference (difference threshold) between the subgroups to determine whether a model is fair or biased. Bias correction can be implemented using a fairness constraint during the model training process. A constraint defines the type of fairness you would like implemented on the sensitive feature during model training, such as demographic parity or equalised odds. It is therefore important to continuously monitor fairness metrics for your models in production, and check for data drift for sensitive subgroups. For this walkthrough, our goal is to identify any kind of bias towards sensitive attributes, and then mitigate that bias during model training. Ensuring your Machine Learning models are fair is much more complex and requires actions across the Machine Learning lifecycle to identify causes and assign appropriate mitigating actions. Just like in the real world, bias within Machine Learning is prominent and should be identified and mitigated in order to treat individuals fairly and prevent our historical biases and prejudices from being fed into algorithms. In this blog, we have covered steps that can be incorporated into the Machine Learning process to first identify and measure fairness, and then to mitigate bias before, during and after model training.

results.title: Bias and Fairness in AI: How to Build Ethical AI Systems
results.content: Bias and fairness in AI refer to the principles and methodologies that ensure artificial intelligence systems treat all individuals equitably, regardless of demographic differences. ## Bias and Fairness in AI: Key Takeaways * Bias in AI stems from flawed data and design choices, impacting the fairness and accuracy of machine learning models, which can lead to harmful outcomes for marginalized groups. * AI fairness depends on identifying potential biases, applying fairness metrics, and ensuring that AI systems remain fair across different demographic groups. * Strategies to mitigate AI bias include using diverse data collection methods, implementing fairness-aware algorithms, and conducting regular audits to promote ethical AI development. Bias within AI systems refers to systemic inequities emerging when machine learning models reinforce and exacerbate historical bias in training data. Additionally, human biases in labeling data and defining fairness metrics can further exacerbate the issue, making ensuring AI systems remain fair across different demographic groups even more challenging. To ensure equitable decision-making through these technologies, efforts must be made to address biases and counteract their effects so that AI fairness is upheld and AI systems remain fair across all applications. To ensure fair AI, it is critical to identify and mitigate algorithmic biases that lead to discriminatory outcomes across different demographic groups. ## Strategies to Reduce AI Bias and Improve Fairness Adopting strategies that diminish AI bias while addressing fairness and enhancing equity is crucial to creating ethical AI systems. ## Conclusion Addressing AI bias is essential for ensuring AI fairness, ethical AI development, and equitable decision-making processes across industries. We can create AI systems that promote fairness rather than reinforce biases by implementing fairness metrics, improving data collection, and refining AI models. AI systems develop bias primarily through the selection and quality of training data, as well as the processes of data collection and labeling. To reduce AI bias and improve fairness, it is essential to utilize diverse data collection methods, implement fairness-aware algorithms, conduct regular audits, and establish ethical guidelines. These strategies, rooted in bias and fairness in AI, promote a more equitable AI system by ensuring that machine learning models minimize bias and provide fair outcomes across different demographic groups.
